judgment: It is good to have somewhere to go.
It is good to see the great person.
image: So the noble one repeats the charge
lines: It is good for a fighting man to hold firm.
with scribes and shamans in hosts.
In the field, three grades of game are caught.
Holding firm: good. Regret gone; nothing unfavourable.
Three days before geng, three days after geng.
his money and his axe are lost.

notes.name_en: 巽 doubled wind trigram, the yielding entry of wind; the thing named, not Wilhelm's 'The Gentle'.
notes.L5: 庚 geng, seventh stem-day (cf. 甲 in 18); the day-names kept where the count matters.
notes.L6: 資斧 money-and-axe — the same stock phrase as 56 L4, kept in the same words.
